header.running_head: Others are Given Preference over the Ansaar in the matter of Khilaafah

blocks.text: Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then stood up and said, "O Assembly of Ansaar! May Allaah reward you all tremendously. May Allaah keep this speaker of yours steadfast. By Allaah! Should you do otherwise (other than what Hadhrat Zaid (RA) has mentioned), we would not reconcile with you." Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) then took hold of the hand of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and said, "This is the man. Pledge your allegiance to him." [^1]

Hadhrat Qaasim bin Muhammad narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away, the Ansaar gathered around Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ubaadah (RA). Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (RA) also arrived there. Hadhrat Hubaab bin Mundhir (RA) who had participated in the Battle of Badr stood up and said, "One leader from you (Muhaajireen) and one from us (Ansaar). O honoured group (of Muhaajireen)! I swear by Allaah that we do not begrudge you this position but we fear that such a person may become the leader whose fathers or brothers we (Ansaar) may have killed (when fighting for Islaam. He should then not wish to take revenge from us)." Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "If it ever happens, you should rather die (fighting him) if you are able to."
Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then started to speak. He said, "We shall be the leaders while you be the viziers. This matter will be shared equally between us just as the frond of a date palm divides at the centre." The first person to pledge his allegiance was Hadhrat Basheer bin Sa'd (also known as) Abu Nu'maan (RA). After everyone had united under the leadership of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), an occasion arrived when he had to distribute some wealth amongst the people. He sent Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) to an old lady from the Banu Adi bin Najaar tribe with her share of the wealth. When she asked what it was, Hadhrat Zaid (RA) told her that it was her share of the wealth that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) had given to the women. She remarked, "Do you wish to bribe me away from my Deen?" "Certainly not," replied Hadhrat Zaid (RA). She then asked, "Do you fear that I shall leave the Deen I follow?" "Definitely not," responded Hadhrat Zaid (RA). She then said, "I swear by Allaah that I shall never accept anything from him in future." When Hadhrat Zaid (RA) returned and informed Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) about what the old lady had expressed, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "We shall also not take back anything that we have given her." [^2]

Tayaalisi, Ibn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.151), Ibn Abi Shayba, Bayhaqi (Vol.8 Pg.134) and others, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.3 Pg.131). Haythami (Vol.5 Pg.183) says that Tabraani and Ahmad have also reported the narration from reliable sources. Tabraani has also reported a similar narration from Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA), as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.3 Pg.140).
Ibn Sa'd and Ibn Jareer, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.3 Pg.130).
